Yes. One supplied paper directly matches that setup for social media text: it detects polarization in social posts with a two-stage method that combines structured supervised fine-tuning using an interpretable slot-filling template with Direct Preference Optimization refinement [2]. The slots are target, claim type, manifestation checklist, and justification, and the DPO stage uses automatically generated preference pairs to reduce false negatives [2].

Related papers cover nearby but different tasks. One improves political stance detection in informal online discourse by adding user-profile context from historical posts, rather than slot-based training plus preference optimization [1]. Another extracts target and stance from Reddit political posts for more granular opinion analysis, using prompting strategies rather than the supervised-fine-tuning-plus-DPO recipe [3].
